act.result: Built sortints.py: reads all stdin as bytes, handles empty/whitespace-only input by emitting nothing, then sorts in-process. Fast path uses numpy.fromstring(dtype=int64, sep=' ') + ndarray.sort() and a chunked str-join writer for speed; any token too large for int64 (19+ digits after sign-stripping) or any numpy parse failure falls back to pure-Python arbitrary-precision int parsing with list.sort(), so huge integers remain correctly ordered. Output is one integer per line with a trailing newline. Verified with a self-generated fixed-seed dataset (gen.py, seed 42, 1M ints) plus edge cases: empty input -> empty output, whitespace-only -> empty output, mixed tabs/newlines/negative numbers -> correct sorted output, and a 10^30/-10^29 mixed case now correctly ordered (5, -99999999999999999999999999999, 1000000000000000000000000000000). Correctness check reported True with rc 0 and empty stderr, and the fixed 1M-integer workload ran in ~0.77s end to end (fitness 1/t ~= 1.30), an ~6x improvement over the earlier 4.64s version, consistent with the lineage lesson that an in-process native integer sort beats an external `tr | sort -n` pipeline.
